A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DP-FedSOFIM and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. The complete 40-page v2 and 59-page v3 support comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original federated image-classification experiments on CIFAR-10 and PathMNIST, including accuracy trajectories for multiple methods, privacy budgets and client counts in Tables 2–3.

after.justification: v3 reports original classification experiments, runtime measurements, component ablations, parameter sensitivity results and statistical comparisons in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The Gaussian release, momentum-based rank-one proxy and Sherman–Morrison update remain. v3 adds an interpolated warm-start variant in Section 3.4.3 and reports using 20 initial EMA-only rounds at ε=0.5, plus bias correction at ε≤1, in Section 5.1. These introduce limited stabilization variants within the retained method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10 and PathMNIST classification. v3 substantially extends the federated test scenarios by adding heterogeneous client label distributions generated with Dirichlet α=0.5. IID evaluation remains in Appendix G, so its movement out of the main text is not a coverage removal.

E2.justification: v2 evaluates DP-FedGD, DP-FedFC and DP-SCAFFOLD. v3 adds DP-FedAvg, DP-FedAdam and DP-FedYogi to the retained IID comparisons, while its non-IID comparisons also include DP-FTRL and DP-AdaFedProx (Tables 3–6 and 8–9). This substantially broadens the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the reported protocol from batch size 64 to full-batch gradients, retains only 20 clients, adds VGG-16 configurations, and removes the non-private and ε=2 evaluations. Fixed SOFIM regularization and momentum become tuned parameters, while clipping becomes fixed at 10. Hyperparameter selection changes from final test accuracy to two-stage, 50-round held-out-validation tuning.

E4.justification: v3 adds component ablations comparing gradient-only, EMA-only and full SOFIM updates, plus a reported ρ-sensitivity sweep (Appendix H, Tables 10–12). Heterogeneity and backbone comparisons expand robustness assessment. Appendix B also adds measured runtime comparisons to the retained analytical complexity discussion.

E5.justification: v2 reports point estimates without run-count or uncertainty information. v3 reports means and standard deviations over three seeds and adds single-seed, continuity-corrected McNemar tests on paired final-round predictions, including disagreement counts and p-values (Appendix J). This newly documents replication and statistical uncertainty; v2 does not establish an earlier run count.

E6.justification: The IID accuracy trajectories are replaced, and non-IID, VGG-16, runtime, ablation and significance results are added. For example, v2 Table 2 reports 65.38% for SOFIM on IID CIFAR-10 with 20 clients at ε=1 and round 70; v3 Table 8 reports 64.39±0.55% under its revised protocol. These results do not establish a same-setting performance decline. The 100-client, non-private and ε=2 result entries disappear.

T1.justification: v3 retains the strong-convexity and PL guarantees but strengthens the preconditioner lower bound and adds a bounded-momentum probability bound, general biased-update descent, a DP-FedGD error-floor comparison, and smooth non-convex stationarity results. Appendix A supplies corresponding new or revised proofs. These substantially extend the formal analysis beyond renumbering existing results.

C1.justification: The empirical contribution is substantially reframed. v2 claims superiority across all budgets and both client scales; v3 emphasizes roughly 4–5 times fewer rounds to target accuracy and best final accuracy in 12 of 16 dataset/backbone/privacy configurations. Cross-backbone claims replace the earlier client-scale emphasis, while the central linear-cost and privacy-preservation claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 attributes early stability to warmup and tuned momentum, interprets adaptive baselines' late catch-up, and discusses conditions where EMA alone largely matches preconditioning. Sections 4.7 and 4.11 explicitly qualify that the theory proves neither a uniformly smaller error floor nor universally improved minimax rates. These substantially revise mechanisms and applicability boundaries, although some overstatements remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly identifies CIFAR-100 pretraining and feature dimensions, supplies expanded search grids and stabilization settings, and documents runtime procedures and per-client class counts. This substantially extends reproducibility information. Some details remain inconsistent: Section 5.1 says IID and non-IID hyperparameters are shared, whereas Appendix G says IID parameters were independently retuned.

R1.justification: v3 expands related work to ADMM and primal-dual federated optimization, including Gong, Möllenhoff, Lan and Zeng, and adds literature supporting the new comparators and statistical analyses. Table 1 and Section 4.11 substantially expand comparative positioning around privacy releases, computational requirements and the limits of theoretical superiority. The SOFIM and DP-FedNew lineage remains.

P1.justification: The experimental analysis, conclusion and discussion are extensively rewritten around early convergence, adaptive comparators and backbone-dependent behavior. The theory is reorganized into additional dedicated subsections, several existing proofs move to Appendix A, and method explanations and pseudocode are revised. This exceeds localized copyediting.

P2.justification: The densely overlaid convergence plots are redesigned into separate privacy-budget panels with uncertainty bands. v3 adds backbone and IID displays, ablation bar charts, and privacy-comparison, runtime, sensitivity, partition and significance tables. Accuracy tables are reorganized around backbone configurations rather than the earlier client-count grouping.

improvement.justification: The decisive gain is replacing v2's test-accuracy-based hyperparameter selection with held-out-validation tuning, addressing an important evaluation weakness. Broader comparators, three-seed uncertainty reporting and component ablations substantially improve the evidence supporting the method, while expanded theory clarifies its guarantees. These gains outweigh the loss of 100-client and two privacy-regime evaluations. Residual inconsistencies temper the improvement, including the PathMNIST-sweep claim contradicted by Table 6 and the misidentification of ρ as EMA decay in Appendix H.2.
